page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.large is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6455B processor with a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. This configuration provides 2 vCPUs from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, supported by a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 60 MB L3 cache. The processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations.

The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not feature local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Driven by the 3.9 GHz clock speed, the instance achieves top-tier single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core scores in the top 10% and single-threaded compression and decompression benchmarks in the top 25%. Conversely, due to the physical core limitation, multi-core benchmarks are weak, with stress-ng multi-core performance in the bottom 10% and Geekbench multi-core scores in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth also shows constraints, with uncached read-only large block bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10%.

Qualitatively, the r7iz.large offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads requiring high-frequency Intel Xeon processing and DDR5 memory without the need for high core density. It is best suited for single-threaded or low-concurrency applications that benefit from high clock speeds and a larger memory footprint per core, such as small-scale relational databases, single-threaded data processing, and lightweight web serving.
